title: Holographic and Immersive Theatre
desc: Plan an immersive or holographic show: concept, stage tech, safety, rights, budget and audience care.
outcomes: Explain holographic effects and immersive formats.
task: Produce a production plan for a short immersive or hologram-style show, with concept, tech list, safety plan, access plan, budget and run sheet.
condition: A computer, a spreadsheet, a venue plan, two peers and a mentor. No live public show is run by learners.
standard: Effects are described accurately (illusion methods named); safety and fire plans approved; access plan included; budget totals correct; peers rate Meets or better.
who: Stage managers, event planners, students, museum staff.
evidence: concept, tech list, safety plan, budget, run sheet
modules: Walk-through rooms, projection mapping, reflected-image effects, VR add-ons.
Most holograms on stage are illusions using angled screens.
A reflected image creates a floating figure.
One idea, one audience, one feeling.
A 5,000-lumen projector suits a small dark room.
Fire exits lit, crowd limits, trip hazards.
Step-free route, seats, captions, audio description.
A performer consent form covers filming.
Equipment hire, crew, venue, marketing, contingency.
Ticket price x seats x shows.
A rehearsal finds a cue 3 seconds late.
quiz: How are many stage holograms made?
rubric: Every claim linked to a dated record and checked by a peer
Checked, dated and explained to others
next: VR live events, podcasting, event management.
local: Public safety and licensing rules differ by place.
ladder: Formats

L1: learner can name formats. Focus module: Formats (Understand, 3 h). Many ways to immerse. Key points: Walk-through rooms, projection mapping, reflected-image effects, VR add-ons. Most holograms on stage are illusions using angled screens. Choose by story and budget.

Teach: open with the worked example. A reflected image creates a floating figure. Then set the activity: Compare 3 formats. Mark against the standard: Table complete. Check at this level: How are many stage holograms made? Model answer: Illusions using angled screens. Formats.
Story and audience
L2: learner knows safety. Focus module: Story and audience (Create, 4 h). Start with the story. Key points: One idea, one audience, one feeling. Map the journey in scenes. Tech serves the story.

Teach: open with the worked example. A six-scene museum walk. Then set the activity: Write a concept. Mark against the standard: One page. Check at this level: Why dark rooms? Model answer: Better visibility. Safety.
Stage tech

L3: learner can list tech. Focus module: Stage tech (Apply, 5 h). Lighting, projection, sound. Key points: Throw distance, brightness (lumens), screen size. Dark rooms improve visibility. Sound sync with cues.

Teach: open with the worked example. A 5,000-lumen projector suits a small dark room. Then set the activity: List equipment. Mark against the standard: Specs listed. Check at this level: Capacity from? Model answer: Exit width. Tech.
Safety
L4: learner can run a rehearsal. Focus module: Safety (Evaluate, 5 h). People in the dark. Key points: Fire exits lit, crowd limits, trip hazards. Flashing lights warnings. Trained staff.

Teach: open with the worked example. Capacity set from exit width. Then set the activity: Write a safety plan. Mark against the standard: Plan approved by venue. Check at this level: Access measure? Model answer: Step-free route or captions. Rehearse.
Access and inclusion

L5: learner can budget. Focus module: Access and inclusion (Evaluate, 4 h). Everyone should enjoy it. Key points: Step-free route, seats, captions, audio description. Low-sensory sessions. Clear signs.

Teach: open with the worked example. Quiet hour with lower sound. Then set the activity: Write an access plan. Mark against the standard: Measures listed. Check at this level: Rights needed for? Model answer: Music, images, performers. Budget.
Budget
L6: learner can lead. Focus module: Budget (Analyse, 4 h). Money plan. Key points: Equipment hire, crew, venue, marketing, contingency. Ticket price x seats x shows. Break-even audience.

Teach: open with the worked example. Break-even 140 seats at 400 INR. Then set the activity: Build a budget. Mark against the standard: Currency shown. Check at this level: Budget contingency? Model answer: Spare funds. Lead.
Run sheet and rehearsal
L7: learner can audit. Focus module: Run sheet and rehearsal (Create, 3 h). Run smoothly. Key points: Cue sheet and roles. Technical and dress rehearsals. Debrief.

Teach: open with the worked example. A rehearsal finds a cue 3 seconds late. Then set the activity: Write a run sheet. Mark against the standard: Complete. Check at this level: Break-even? Model answer: Audience to cover cost. Peer audit.
